ABSTRACT  
Biomass - derived carbon electrode material with a porous structure is widely used in supercapacitor applica -
tions, which can improve electron transfer and shorter ion diffusion pathways. In this work, the garlic peel 
biomass carbon (GPBC), NiMo
3
S
4
(NMS) and garlic peel biomass carbon decorated with NiMo
3
S
4 
(GPBC/NMS) 
composite were prepared through a in situ two-step hydrothermal method. The synthesized materials were 
characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD) and field emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM), energy 
dispersive x-ray spectroscopy (EDS), Transmission electron microscopy techniques (TEM), Raman spectroscopy 
and Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) techniques were used to analyze the structure, morphology and specific 
surface areas and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). The prepared bimetallic metal sulfide on a biomass - 
derived carbon namely the GPBC/NMS composite is used in supercapacitor application. The GPBC/NMS com -
posite electrode exhibits good cycle performance with high specific capacity of 304C/g at current density of 1 A/ 
g in a 3 M KOH electrolyte solution. The electrochemical performance of the GPBC/NMS//GPBC asymmetric 
supercapacitor device produces an excellent energy density 45.5 Wh kg
� 1 
at a power density of 1125 W kg
� 1 
in 
the 1.6 V operating potential window. The GPBC/NMS//GPBC also exhibits 93 % retention of its initial 
capacitance after the 10,000 GCD cycle performance. The above results demonstrate a new way of developing 
high performance electrode materials for energy storage applications.   
1. Introduction 
In today's world, the consumption of fossil energy for portable 
electronic devices, electronic vehicles, and other energy-consuming 
industrialization are increasing day by day and the demand of the en -
ergy causing environmental pollution and economic issues. [ 1 , 2 ]. With 
the increase in necessity for energy, it becomes necessary to store energy 
and use it efficiently. Advanced energy storage devices such as fuel 
batteries, supercapacitors and rechargeable batteries have been suc -
cessfully relieve environmental problems and energy shortage [ 3 , 4 ]. 
Among the advanced energy storage systems, Supercapacitors are the 
main energy storage system that has attracted more attention due to 
their long cycling stability, extremely low internal resistance, high 
power density capability, fast charge-discharge cycling, and longer life 
span [ 5 ]. The supercapacitor is mainly classified into three groups ac -
cording to the energy storage mechanism: Electrode double layer ca -
pacitors (EDLC), Pseudocapacitors, and Hybrid capacitors. In recent 
years, the combination of EDLC and pseudocapacitor in the hybrid 
capacitor has attracted attention due to its high performance, good 
cycling stability, and excellent specific capacitance [ 6 – 8 ]. 
The hybrid supercapacitor is largely dependent on the nature of 
Electrodes, electrolyte, separators and current collectors. The carbon 
based electrodes such as carbon nanotube (CNT), carbon nanofiber, 
graphene, activated carbon (AC), carbon aerogel, etc. are considered to 
be the ideal electrode materials in the supercapacitor because of their 
physiochemical properties such as high chemical stability, high specific 
surface area, excellent electrical conductivity, etc. [ 9 – 11 ]. In recent 
years, biomass-derived carbon materials synthesized from various

biomasses, including banana peel [ 12 ] corncob [ 13 ], rice husk [ 14 ], 
lotus stem [ 15 ], bamboo [ 16 ], pomelo peel [ 17 ], tobacco waste [ 18 ], 
pencil peel [ 19 ] and etc., have been used as carbon sources to prepare 
carbon materials for energy storage applications. Biomass-derived car -
bon materials have the advantages of a rich carbon content, high specific 
surface area, an enlarged pore structure, and excellent electrical con -
ductivity, making them suitable for use as electrode materials in 
supercapacitor applications [ 20 – 22 ]. Utilizing biomass waste as an 
electrode sources to create abundant electroactive sites carbon with 
enhanced EDLC supercapacitor performance due to their hierarchical 
meso/micro pores and presence of various heteroatoms. To develop 
hybrid super capacitor, the effective pseudo behavior nanomaterial's are 
composed with biomass derived carbon [ 23 ]. Hybridization of transition 
metal oxides on the surface of the carbon material is enhance the elec -
trochemical performance and makes synergistic effect that takes ad -
vantages in energy storage applications. To date, high-performance 
electrodes have undergone intensive exploration and exploitation to 
meet the aforementioned demands, such as metal oxides, metal sulfides, 
metal phosphides, and so on. Specifically, transition metal sulfides 
(TMSs) have received significant attention due to their superior con -
ductivity and remarkable electrochemical performance due to their 
pseudo capacitive ability [ 24 , 25 ]. Extensive research has been carried 
out to study the high theoretical specific capacity of binary transition 
metal sulfides and their use as supercapacitor electrode materials [ 26 ]. 
Furthermore, despite its attractive electrochemical properties, the TMS 
is exhibited low specific capacity. To overcome the problem, the new 
strategy method is used to increase the specific capacitance of TMS 
materials. Due to the high charge transfer resistance and low efficiency 
of the active material, the practical specific capacity of TMS is currently 
quite low in comparison to its theoretical value [ 27 ]. In the TMS ma -
terials, NiCo
2
S
4 
is mostly examined by supercapacitors because of their 
high theoretical capacitance, low cost, and easy synthesis process. Some 
reports on NiMo
3
S
4 
battery-type materials were investigated by super -
capacitor applications [ 28 , 29 ]. Research investigations required to find 
suitable composites along with TMS for enhanced electrochemical per -
formance and redox ability through synergistic effect [ 30 , 31 ]. 
In this work, the novel NiMo
3
S
4 
embedded heteroatom doped carbon 
using natural garlic peel waste derived carbon support as support to 
enhance the conductivity of NiMo
3
S
4 
in order to fabricate super -
capacitor. Garlic peel derived activated carbon was decorated with 
NiMo
3
S
4
(GPBC/NMS) through an in situ two-step hydrothermal process 
for energy storage applications. The GPBC was prepared by the hydro -
thermal method and activated by KOH with a developed pore structure 
to improve the conductive substrate of NMS, which could potentially 
enhance the electrochemical performance of the GPBC/NMS composite. 
In addition, the asymmetric supercapacitor assembled with GPBC/NMS 
for the positive electrode and GPBC for the negative electrode could 
produce excellent electrochemical performance. The strategy suggested 
here may inspire new possibility of sustainably producing biomass 
derived carbon materials for advanced energy storage.

2.4. Characterization method 
Various characterization techniques were used to characterize the 
synthesized materials. The crystal structure of synthesized samples was 
characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern were using Shimadzu

scanning range of 2 θ = 10 – 80
◦

thesized samples were examined by field emission scanning electron 
microscopy (FESEM)using a Quanta feg 250 instrument and High Res -
olution Transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM)and energy disper -

instrument. Raman spectra of the samples were recorded by using a 
confocal Raman spectrometer (WITec, Germany). To analyze the 
textural properties, the nitrogen (N
2

Emmett-Teller (BET) methods. The electronic state of the elements in the 
prepared composite was evaluated by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy 
(XPS) analysis with a PHI Versaprobe III instrument.

4. Electrochemical study on synthesized materials 
The electrochemical performance of as-synthesized NMS and GPBC/ 
NMS composite electrode materials was investigated by a three- 
electrode configuration using 3 M KOH as aqueous electrolyte solu -
tion. Fig. 6 (a) show the CV curves of GPBC, NMS, and GPBC/NMS 
electrodes recorded at 30 mV/s within the potential window of � 0.2 to 
0.5 V. The CV curve of GPBC has a quasi-rectangular shape which is 
indicating the EDLC behavior of carbon material. Fig. 6 (b-c) shows the 
CV curves of NMS and GPBC/NMS electrodes with various scan rates in 
the range of 10 – 50 mV/s. Every CV graphs showed that each sample has 
a redox peaks shows that the typical pseudocapacitive characteristics of 
the metal sulfide electrodes. As the scanning rate increases, the oxida -
tion and reduction peaks shifted towards negative and positive poten -
tials. This occurred because of the ion diffusion rate needed, to decrease 
the electronic neutralization in the redox process. At a slow scan rate, 
the OH ions effectively interacted with both the inner and outer surfaces 
of the electrodes due to the adequate time available. Conversely, at a 
high scan rate, the OH � ions had limited time to intercalate with the 
electrode surfaces [ 48 ]. Fig. S2a) exhibit the CV curves of GPBC at 
various scan rate in the range of 10 – 100 mV/S. The CV curves of GPBC/

The GPBC/NMS composite electrode has a longer discharge time than 
the NMS electrode at the same current density, indicating the composite 
electrode has a higher capacity than NMS electrode respectively. Fig. 7 
(b-c) shows the GCD curves of NMS and GPBC/NMS composite elec -
trodes at different current densities ranging from 1 to 5 A/g. All GCD 
curves and their shapes are maintained same, even at high current

decreases because of the fast-absorbing electrolyte ions on the active 
material surface. As a result, the improved electrochemical performance 
arises from the synergetic effect due to the increases the active sites of 
GPBC by intercalation of NMS enhances the interface response with the 
electrode and electrolyte interface and improve the electrical conduc -
tance. The specific capacity variation of NMS and GPBC/NMS compos -
ites is exhibited in Fig. 7 (d).The GCD curves of GPBC electrode at 
different current densities ranging from 1 to 5 A/g exhibited in Fig. S5. 
The electrochemical impedance spectroscopy analysis was carried out in 
a frequency range of 1 MHz to 0.1 Hz. Fig. 8 (a) shows the Nyquist plot of 
the prepared electrode materials, and their plots exhibit a semi-circle in 
the high frequency region and a straight line that is nearly parallel to the 
imaginary component. Fig. 8 a shows the GPBC/NMS electrode has 
semicircle in the high-frequency region is shorter than the NMS elec -
trode, which causes low resistance and high diffusion of ions to the 
electrode surface from the electrolyte. The GPBC/NMS composite has a 
lower semicircle than the NMS electrode, which indicates the GPBC/ 
NMS has good charge transfer property and superior electrical conduc -
tivity. Fig. 8 b shows the long-term cycling stability of the GPBC/NMS 
composite with 10,000 cycles at a 5 A/g current density in a 3 M KOH 
electrolyte. After completing the 10,000 galvanostatic charge-discharge 
cycles, the composite electrode retained 90 % of its initial capacitance. 
These results show the GPBC/NMS has demonstrated excellent stability 
and good rate capability. 
4.1. Electrochemical properties of two electrode system 
The electrochemical superior performance of the GPBC/NMS com -
posite in three electrode configuration was investigated for real life 
application as redox feature electrode material to build an asymmetric 
supercapacitor device. In a two electrode configured systems, the GPBC/ 
NMS//GPBC was assembled using the GPBC/NMS as the positive elec -
trode, the GPBC as the negative electrode with 3 M KOH aqueous elec -
trolyte. We assembled the asymmetric two-electrode configuration 
based on a positive electrode of GPBC/NMS composite and a negative 
electrode of GPBC material in a 3 M KOH electrolyte. Fig. 9 a) shows the 
schematic illustration of the assembled asymmetric supercapacitor cell 
and the operating potential window has demonstrated by cyclic vol -
tammetry studies of GPBC/NMS composite and GPBC in a three- 
electrode system. The asymmetric supercapacitor device refers to the 
sum of positive and negative electrode potential. All the CV curves 
exhibit quasi rectangular shape which is demonstrating the EDLC 
behavior. Fig. 9 b) shows the GPBC/NMS composite and GPBC electrodes 
at a scan rate of 50 mV/s, and the corresponding potential windows are 
0 to 1.6 V and 0 to -1 V respectively. The working voltage range of 
GPBC/NMS//GPBC asymmetric device was 0 – 1.6 V. Fig. 9 c) shows the 
CV curves of an asymmetric device GPBC/NMS//GPBC at various po -
tential windows at 50 mV/s scan rate. All the CV curves of asymmetric 
device exists a combination of EDLC and pseudocapacitance character -
istics from GPBC and NMS electrode materials, which indicates rapid ion 
transfer behavior and good reversibility. Fig. 9 d) exhibits the asym -
metric device at various scan rates ranging from 10 to 50 mV/s in the 
0 – 1.6 V. Fig. 9 e) exhibits the GCD curves of GPBC/NMS//GPBC asym -
metric devices in different operating potential windows ranging from 
1.0 to 1.6 V at 1 A/g current density. Every GCD curves that displays a 
linear triangle shape indicates good electrochemical performance in the 
asymmetric capacitor. Fig. 9 f) shows the GCD curves of asymmetric 
device at different current densities ranging from 1 to 5 A/g in the po -
tential window of 0 – 1.6 V. Even with high current density applied, the 
GCD nonlinear curves maintain symmetrical shape without distortion 
due to faradic and non- faradic reactions of positive and negative elec -
trodes that can be carried out in supercapacitor cell, indicating that the 
GPBC/NMS//GPBC asymmetric device has good specific capacity and 
high reversibility performance. To estimate the performance of the 
asymmetric supercapacitor device, the energy and power density were 
very crucial parameters. Fig. 9 g) shows the ragone plot of the GPBC/ 
NMS//GPBC asymmetric device. The Ragone plot of high energy density 
at high power density confirms the ability of devices to charge and 
discharge with high specific capacitance. Fig. 9 g) shows the Ragone plot

5. Conclusion 
In conclusion, the GPBC was successfully prepared using waste garlic 
peel biomass raw material. The GPBC/NMS composite was synthesized 
by the facile hydrothermal method at 180 
◦
C for 12 h. The synthesized 
materials were characterized by various characterization techniques. In 
the three-electrode system, NMS was decorated on the GPBC surface of 
the GPBC/NMS composite to enhance the capacity performance, and it 
has a high capacity of 304 C/g at 1 A/g current density. Furthermore, an 
assembled asymmetric supercapacitor was fabricated with GPBC/NMS 
and GPBC as the positive and negative electrodes, respectively. The 
asymmetric supercapacitor device GPBC/NMS//GPBC exhibits a high 
energy density of 45.5 Wh kg
� 1 
with a power density of 1125 W kg
� 1 
at 
1 A/g current density, respectively. Moreover, the asymmetric device 
has excellent stability, as it is able to retain 93 % of its specific capacity 
even after 10,000 charging-discharging cycles. Therefore, the above 
results were demonstrated that the biomass-derived GPBC material as a 
conductive substrate to support the bimetallic sulfide NMS active ma -
terials will be a promising electrode for developing high-performance 
asymmetric supercapacitor applications.
